title: Acid Nucleic Extraction from Rice Dried Leaves
author: Martine Bangratz
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bcntiven
materials: Grind the dried leaves with the Qiagen TissueLyser II until obtaining a fine powder

steps.title: Add CTAB buffer and vortex
steps.instruction: Add 1 ml CTAB extraction buffer (as defined in the “before start” section) to the dried rice leaf sample and homogenize by vortexing.

steps.title: Incubate and centrifuge lysate
steps.instruction: Incubate the homogenate at 65 °C for 30 minutes, mixing the tubes gently periodically; then centrifuge at 10 000 × g, 4 °C for 10 minutes.

substeps.instruction: Incubate at 65 °C for 30 min with gentle mixing.

steps.title: Extract with chloroform/isoamyl alcohol
steps.instruction: Transfer 650 µl of the supernatant to a 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tube, add 650 µl chloroform/isoamyl alcohol (24:1), mix by shaking, then centrifuge at 15 000 × g, 4 °C for 10 minutes.

substeps.instruction: Transfer 650 µl supernatant to a new 1.5 ml tube.
Add an equal volume (650 µl) of chloroform/isoamyl alcohol (24:1).

steps.title: Precipitate DNA with isopropanol
steps.instruction: Transfer 500 µl of the resulting supernatant to a fresh 1.5 ml tube containing 350 µl pre‑chilled (‑20 °C) isopropanol, mix gently, incubate at ‑20 °C for 30 minutes, then centrifuge at 15 000 × g, 4 °C for 10 minutes.

substeps.instruction: Transfer 500 µl supernatant to a new tube.
Add 350 µl isopropanol that has been pre‑chilled at ‑20 °C.

steps.title: Wash pellet with 70% ethanol
steps.instruction: Discard the supernatant, wash the DNA pellet with 70 % ethanol, and centrifuge at 15 000 × g for 5 minutes (temperature not specified).

substeps.instruction: Add 70 % ethanol to the pellet and mix.

steps.title: Air‑dry pellet
steps.instruction: Remove the ethanol completely and allow the pellet to air‑dry.

steps.title: Resuspend DNA and store
steps.instruction: Dissolve the dried pellet in 50 µl sterile water or TE buffer and store the DNA at ‑20 °C.
